name: blue-down
prompt:
Make EIGHT coherent whole-character frames of blue CHRONOS, a 4-column 2-row sprite sheet on transparent background. Reference1 is the APPROVED rigid-hammer key pose set, mandatory geometry and identity. Reference2 is the EXACT canonical metal T hammer design; keep its ONE STRAIGHT shaft welded perpendicularly into CYLINDER SIDE MIDPOINT, NEVER an elbow, bend, rubber mallet, parallel offset shaft, shaft growing from an endcap, or shaft through both sides. Both armored fists close together on the SAME straight shaft on the SAME side of cylinder. Reference3 is the approved starting/carry sequence, use its ready grip/armor, but never reproduce a malformed weapon. Draw coherent COMPLETE character plus held weapon, not assembled or cutout parts. Same figure proportions/body size in all 8 cells, full closed finned black helmet with narrow cyan visor; heavy charcoal/silver armor, blue accents and circular cyan chest core. Face/torso remain toward viewer while shoulders hinge/twist naturally. Physically same fixed rigid head and haft throughout; ALL perspective changes affect the ENTIRE hammer together. Preserve barrel diameter and shaft length. Metallic black/silver flat rings and blue lightning body, round cyan inset endcaps.
Crisp detailed 16-bit pixel-art sprites, not blurry. ALL 8 have complete head/helmet/fins/hammer/boots and 30px transparent margin within their equal cells, NO clipping, no trails, shadows, particles, labels or background. Landscape 4x2 sheet. Feet at same baseline per row; model scale remains constant; bending knees can lower actual torso. Animate ONLY the overhead DOWNSWING from approved key1 to key4 in row-major order, genuine incremental whole poses:
0 maximal overhead windup like ref1 top-left, hands above forehead on straight haft, head points toward camera IN DEPTH, showing near ROUND endcap and barrel receding upward; this is NOT a vertical cylinder with an offset parallel shaft.
1 begin pull forward, slight shoulder/hip rotation, head advances in depth.
2 high downstroke, straight shaft now diagonally down-right to hands, head still above-left forehead, near endcap visible as in ref1 top-right.
3 accelerating, hands descend across upper chest, head leads forward-left, body starts hinge.
4 deep forward stroke, head in front-left at knees, BOTH fists together around straight shaft at waist. Head axis rotates with whole hammer, no bent joint.
5 almost impact, cylinder becoming UPRIGHT in front-left below knee level, lower flat cap points down, shaft goes diagonally BACK/UP-RIGHT from its side MIDPOINT to hands at right waist.
6 definite planted impact EXACTLY like ref1 bottom-right: barrel upright, flat BOTTOM end cap touching ground in front-left of boots, shaft a single uninterrupted STRAIGHT diagonal line back/up-right to both hands, head undistorted. Feet brace, knees bent, torso forward.
7 separate follow-through body compression after contact, head remains solid unmoved on same ground point, two fists and shaft stay connected, no shortening or bending. Preserve same head design/size even under impact.
